title_en: Urgent Notice of the Supreme People's Court on Effectively Preventing Debtors from Evading Debts in the Trial of Enterprise Bankruptcy and Restructuring Cases by People's Courts
keywords_en: bankruptcy; in the trial of enterprise bankruptcy and restructuring cases
full_text_en:
Supreme People's Court

Urgent Notice on Effectively Preventing Debtors from Evading Debts in the Trial of Enterprise Bankruptcy and Restructuring Cases by People's Courts

Fa [2001] No. 105

To: High People's Courts of all provinces, autonomous regions, and municipalities directly under the Central Government; the Military Court of the People's Liberation Army; and the Production and Construction Corps Branch of the High People's Court of the Xinjiang Uygur Autonomous Region:

In order to ensure strict application of the law, accurate grasp of policy boundaries, resolute resistance and elimination of local protectionism interference, and effective prevention of the phenomenon of evading and suspending debts in the trial of enterprise bankruptcy and restructuring cases, the following urgent notice is hereby given on several issues to which people's courts should pay special attention in the current trial of enterprise bankruptcy and restructuring cases:

1. The trial of enterprise bankruptcy and restructuring cases by people's courts is an important aspect of using judicial means to maintain the market economic order and social credit, and to promote economic system reform and economic development. People's courts at all levels must be guided by Comrade Jiang Zemin's important thought of the "Three Represents," raise awareness, strengthen leadership, deploy judges with strong political integrity and professional competence to proactively and prudently adjudicate every enterprise bankruptcy and restructuring case. Court leaders must personally attend to these matters. Courts with heavy trial workloads should organize dedicated collegial panels. Intermediate and High People's Courts shall keep abreast of the circumstances of significant cases within their jurisdictions, and report typical cases and major issues to the superior people's court in a timely manner.

2. Superior people's courts shall effectively strengthen supervision and guidance over the trial of enterprise bankruptcy cases by lower people's courts. Where a ruling declaring enterprise bankruptcy is indeed erroneous, the superior court shall notify the lower court to correct it according to law, and if necessary, may instruct the lower court to make a new ruling. After the bankruptcy declaration, if a creditor or debtor raises an objection, they may apply for reconsideration to the people's court at the next higher level within ten days from the date of the bankruptcy declaration by the people's court. The higher-level people's court shall make a reconsideration decision within fifteen days.

3. People's courts should be cautious in accepting enterprise bankruptcy cases for filing. If, upon examination of the bankruptcy application, there are indications of debt evasion, or insufficient evidence of "insolvency," the applicant shall be ordered to supplement materials, and the case shall not be blindly filed. Where it is discovered that a debtor has a huge amount of property with an unknown whereabouts and the debtor cannot reasonably explain the property's whereabouts, or the debtor first strips effective assets to form another company and then applies for bankruptcy, the bankruptcy application shall be dismissed by ruling. For bankruptcy applications of domestic trade and foreign trade enterprises, strict compliance with the approval procedure requirements of the Guo Jing Mao (1996) No. 492 document shall be observed, with strict control and prudent acceptance.

4. When trying enterprise bankruptcy cases, people's courts shall effectively supervise and guide the liquidation group to carefully examine the bankruptcy enterprise's financial statements and original vouchers, verify creditors' rights and debts item by item, and maximize the protection of the legitimate rights and interests of creditors and other parties. Acts by the bankrupt enterprise such as concealing, privately distributing, and transferring property without compensation, selling property at reduced prices, as well as提前清偿未到期债务 in violation of law to the detriment of other creditors' interests, and waiving claims, shall be confirmed void according to law, or revoked upon application of the parties according to law, and effective measures shall be taken to recover property to prevent the loss of state-owned assets. The policy boundaries shall be accurately grasped. For bankruptcy of state-owned industrial enterprises not included in the "National Enterprise Merger, Bankruptcy and Employee Re-employment Work Plan," the documents Guo Fa (1994) No. 59 and (1997) No. 10 of the State Council shall not apply. Instead, the matter shall be handled in accordance with the provisions of the "Enterprise Bankruptcy Law of the People's Republic of China (For Trial Implementation)," i.e., the proceeds from the realization of the bankrupt enterprise's property must be used to repay debts on a pro rata basis. The expenses for resettling employees of the bankrupt enterprise can only be properly addressed through channels such as local government subsidies, civil relief, and social security. It is strictly forbidden and shall be corrected any phenomenon of violating regulations, arbitrarily "hitching a ride," and impairing the legitimate interests of creditors. For state-owned enterprise bankruptcy cases included in the national merger and bankruptcy plan, before the bankruptcy property has been lawfully liquidated and disposed of, the bankruptcy proceedings shall not be concluded by ruling.

5. When disposing of bankruptcy property, auction methods shall generally be adopted, and supervision over the auction process shall be strengthened. The transparency and fairness of the auction shall be ensured to prevent the auction from becoming a mere formality. The qualifications of bidders shall be determined according to law; except as clearly provided by laws, regulations, and relevant policies, bidders shall not be arbitrarily restricted. The price of the auctioned bankruptcy property shall be based on the appraisal-determined price, and the reserve price shall be determined in accordance with relevant state regulations. If the auction fails on the first attempt, the reserve price shall be lowered and the auction shall continue. If a transaction still cannot be concluded, the property may be appraised in kind to offset debts upon discussion and approval by the creditors' meeting or by ruling of the people's court. When offsetting debts with in-kind appraisals, the last auction reserve price shall be used as the basic basis to achieve fairness and justice. It shall be prevented that the use of inappropriate in-kind distribution methods to offset bankruptcy claims impairs the interests of creditors.

6. The validity of guarantees provided by the bankrupt enterprise shall be carefully examined and confirmed strictly in accordance with the law and judicial interpretations. The validity of a guarantee contract shall not be denied merely because the guarantee was given at the direction of the government in contravention of the guarantor's will, or because the guarantor has no property to bear the guarantee liability. Still less shall the guarantor's liability for compensation be completely exempted after the guarantee contract is confirmed invalid. If a debtor has multiple ordinary creditors and the debtor, in malicious collusion with one of the creditors, mortgages all or part of its property to that creditor, thereby losing the ability to perform other debts and impairing the legitimate rights and interests of other creditors, the impaired creditors may request the people's court to revoke such mortgage act, and the people's court shall support this according to law. For lawful and valid mortgages, it shall be ensured that the mortgagee has priority in repayment.

7. When trying cases of disputes arising from the restructuring of state-owned enterprises, including enterprise company system transformation, joint-stock cooperative system reform, debt-to-equity swaps, sale of small state-owned enterprises, enterprise merger and division, people's courts shall strictly apply the law and national restructuring policies. Where relevant laws and administrative regulations contain no explicit provisions, the normative documents of the relevant competent department under the State Council in effect at the time of the restructuring act may be applied. Local restructuring documents that violate laws, administrative regulations, and policies stipulated by the State Council shall not be used as a basis for handling cases.

8. When trying state-owned enterprise restructuring cases, if the normative documents of the relevant competent department under the State Council in effect at the time of the restructuring act explicitly require approval procedures, and such approval procedures have not been fulfilled and have not been subsequently completed, or if both parties have maliciously colluded to harm the interests of the state or creditors, the relevant agreement shall be confirmed void according to law. In the sale of small enterprises, if the seller uses the sale to evade debts and the transferee is aware of this, the creditor's claim to revoke the enterprise sale contract shall be supported according to law.

9. When trying state-owned enterprise restructuring cases, people's courts shall lawfully and properly handle the issue of assuming the legacy debts of the restructured enterprise. For legacy debts of the restructured enterprise, if the parties have agreed on a new debt bearer and the creditors have consented, the parties' agreement may be followed. If, although the creditors have not consented, the new debt bearer has sufficient ability to repay the debts, it may be confirmed according to the actual circumstances that the new debt bearer shall bear the debts. If only the property of the restructured enterprise has been disposed of but the debts of the restructured enterprise have not been handled by the relevant person, in principle, the restructured enterprise shall bear the legacy debts of the original enterprise to the extent of the value of the property it has received.

10. When trying state-owned enterprise restructuring cases, if the seller conceals or omits the original enterprise's debts in the sale of the enterprise, the seller shall be liable to the original enterprise's creditors for the concealed or omitted debts. If, during the joint-stock cooperative system reform or merger by absorption of an enterprise, the original asset manager of the merged or restructured enterprise conceals or omits debts, the original asset manager of the merged or restructured enterprise shall bear civil liability for the concealed or omitted debts. If an enterprise is divided to strip effective assets in order to evade debts, the divided enterprises shall be named as co-defendants, and it shall be confirmed according to law that they bear joint and several liability.

Upon receipt of this notice, immediately organize relevant trial judges to study it, promptly conduct a thorough review of the cases being tried in your jurisdiction, and formulate implementation measures to effectively prevent the problem of debtors evading debts in the trial of enterprise bankruptcy and restructuring cases. The status of the review and implementation shall be promptly reported to the Supreme People's Court.

August 10, 2001
